title: 168 of 336 photos have no bytes anywhere (50%) -- the NAS fallback root and ActiveStorage are both dead, so nothing protects the live corpus from the same loss
evidence:
168 of 336 photos (50%) have no bytes anywhere reachable, and every one of them is permanently unpostable. Measured 2026-09-20 from the live DB + filesystem:
- servable_file_path is nil for 168/336 photos; the two sources it knows are BOTH dead for them: `path` does not exist and the NAS fallback root is gone.
- The NAS fallback root in ContentPillars::Photo::NAS_OUTPUT_BASE ('/mnt/synology-home/backup/essdee/ComfyUI') DOES NOT EXIST: /mnt/synology-home is an empty directory (2 entries, root-owned), not a mount. The fallback has therefore never resolved for any photo.
- /mnt/essdee (the original ComfyUI output mount the photos' `path` points at) is now an EMPTY directory and is not in `mount` output at all -- 101 photos carry a path under it.
- ActiveStorage is NOT a second source either: config.active_storage.service = :local for both dev and production (Disk service rooted at storage/, 116K total), and 0 of the 101 attached-but-local-dead photos have a present blob file (blob.service.exist?(blob.key) == false for all 101). `image.attached?` is a RECORD, not bytes.
- The only surviving mirror, /mnt/nas-ai-models/comfyui-output (114,006 files), recovers 0 of the 168 by basename -- those legacy bytes are simply gone.
- This is not hypothetical harm: 58 of the 64 failed posts reference a photo whose bytes are gone, and 109 posted rows reference one (posted when B2 still served them).

Impact now: DORMANT but permanent. The selector no longer offers dead photos (fixed this run -- Photos::ListAvailable now selects on ContentPillars::Photo#servable_bytes?), and the queue is filled by the render path, so nothing is failing today. What is NOT fixed: (a) the redundancy gap that caused it -- every current photo is served from a single local file on /mnt/fscache (an encrypted volume), so the same loss is one unmount away for the whole live corpus; (b) NAS_OUTPUT_BASE is dead code that will not protect any future photo whose local file disappears.

Fix direction (needs a decision, not a blind edit): repoint the fallback only with a COLLISION-SAFE mapping -- a basename glob in a 114k-file tree can serve the WRONG image, which is worse than 404 -- and/or give renders a real second copy (the harness already writes to /mnt/fscache/essdee/ComfyUI/output/gen-*.png, which the NAS mirror also holds; a verified copy step at render time would restore redundancy).

notes.note: 2026-09-20 11:3xZ ops-triage: the headline claim was WRONG, and the defect behind it is FIXED. (1) MEASURED: the render output tree is served through a symlink -- /mnt/fscache/essdee/ComfyUI/output -> /mnt/nas-ai-models/comfyui-output (same inode 19373054 via both paths) -- so the live corpus's bytes are on the NAS, not only on the encrypted fscache volume. (2) 101 of the 168 'no bytes anywhere' photos were NEVER lost: their bytes sit at the same RELATIVE path under the NAS mirror, verified for all 101 (photo 26 -> sarah1a3/fashion/962260888105743/image_00002_.png, 2692215 bytes; photos 8-113). The earlier '0 of 168 recoverable' came from matching by BASENAME in a mirror holding thousands of image_00002_.png files. (3) ROOT CAUSE: ContentPillars::Photo#servable_file_path fell back to NAS_OUTPUT_BASE = /mnt/synology-home/backup/essdee/ComfyUI -- a noauto CIFS mount that is normally NOT mounted (/mnt/synology-home is an empty root-owned dir) -- and its prefix test knew only the ORIGINAL /mnt/essdee/ComfyUI mount, so photos imported from the CURRENT mount had NO fallback while the fallback that existed could never resolve. FIXED: the resolver strips any known ComfyUI-output prefix and retries under Photo::MIRROR_ROOTS (real, existing roots), direct path first; the ambiguous bare-basename glob was removed (it could serve a DIFFERENT photo's bytes). (4) VERIFIED: 101/101 legacy photos resolve; photo 350 (live) still resolves by its direct path; spec/models/content_pillars_photo_resolution_spec.rb 7 examples 0 failures; full suite 395 examples 0 failures 8 pending; new probe check check_photo_resolution measures the resolver against the mirror INDEPENDENTLY of its own constants -- live: roots exist, 0 stranded; with the prefix stubbed broken: 101 stranded (ids 8,9,10,11,12), i.e. it would have caught this defect. (5) NOT a content change: the recovered 101 are all already referenced by terminal posts (43 posted, 58 failed), so the candidate pool is unchanged at 51 -- reachability, not eligibility. RESIDUAL moved to photo-corpus-single-copy: 66 photos are genuinely gone (mostly /tmp/gen_*.png renders whose bytes never reached a durable mount), and the corpus has exactly one copy.
